newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Most Argentines sympathetic to general strike-poll.
newsitem.headline: Most Argentines sympathetic to general strike-poll.

text.p: Most Argentines favor with a 36-hour general strike set to begin midday Thursday, according to private polls published Wednesday.
According to a survey by pollsters Graciela Romer y Asociados printed by La Nacion, 54 percent of Argentines are in favor of the stoppage, while 27 percent oppose it and 19 percent were undecided.
But only 30 percent of respondents said they would join the strike, while another 24 percent said they would attend demonstrations but go to work as well.
A survey by Ricardo Rouvier printed in Pagina 12 showed that 69 percent favor the strike, 25 percent were against, and six percent without opinion.
Pagina 12 said the survey showed much higher support for the strike than for the last, 24-hour, stoppage in August.

Other figures from Rouvier, published by El Cronista, showed that 55 percent of those who supported the strike would actually stop work. This means that 38 percent of those surveyed by Rouvier intended to join in the stoppage.

The image of the Peronist Party government of President Carlos Menem also continues to slide, according to another Rouvier poll in El Cronista. Only 14 percent of respondents in September said they had a good or very good impression of the government, compared with 18 percent in July and 35 percent at the time of presidential elections in May 1995.

El Cronista said that 897 people told Rouvier that they agreed with the strike, but the newspapers gave no other details on the number of people in the surveys, when they were taken, or their margin of error.

The strike is being led by the CGT union confederation, which is usually close to the Peronists. But, angered by unemployment of 17.1 percent, it is fighting Menem's drive for fiscal austerity and more flexible labor laws.
